name: Tessera Industries Data Spike DS-1 'Upload'
description: A wrist-mounted penetrating spike connected to the user's neural interface that physically punctures a target's cyberware housing and establishes a direct hardline connection to their implant network. The spike is a 6cm retractable carbon-ceramic needle containing a fiber-optic data conduit that can transmit attack payloads directly into a target's neural architecture, bypassing wireless security protocols entirely. The physical penetration is painful but rarely dangerous — the data payload is where the real damage occurs. Operators use it to inject malware, extract data, override motor functions, or in extreme cases, trigger a neural interface hard reset that can cause permanent cognitive damage.
specifications:
spike length: 6 cm retractable
spike material: Carbon-ceramic with fiber-optic core
penetration depth: Sufficient for standard cyberware housing
data transfer rate: 40 Gbps through fiber-optic conduit
deployment: Wrist-mounted spring mechanism, 0.1 second extension
weight: 0.12 kg total assembly
compatibility: Requires user neural interface for payload delivery
story_hooks: A victim was found with a DS-1 puncture wound but no data payload was delivered — the spike was used purely as a physical weapon, suggesting the attacker wanted it to look like a cyber attack.
A new payload circulating for DS-1 users doesn't attack the target — it copies their entire neural interface memory buffer, stealing the last 48 hours of sensory experience.
related_entities: CortexDynamics Apex Drive Performance Neural BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek wrist-mounted apparatus resembling a modified smartband with a recessed spike chamber. The device has a minimalist, clinical aesthetic—all function, no decoration. At rest, only a subtle metallic seam marks the spike's housing along the inner wrist. When deployed, a translucent carbon-ceramic needle extends with predatory precision.
physical_description.dimensions: Wrist band: 18cm circumference × 3.2cm width × 1.8cm depth. Spike projection: 6cm length when extended, 0.4cm diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Remarkably light and balanced—barely noticeable on the wrist until deployed, then the mechanical tension in the spring mechanism creates a sense of coiled potential. Feels like wearing a high-end prosthetic rather than a weapon.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polymer frame with carbon-ceramic spike assembly. Fiber-optic conduit runs through the spike's hollow core. Contact pads are surgical-grade stainless steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents. The spike chamber has a slight iridescent sheen from the embedded fiber-optic bundling visible through semi-translucent ceramic housing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with brushed silver contact pads. The spike interior shows faint rainbow refraction from the fiber-optic core when light hits it at certain angles.
physical_description.grip_texture: The wrist band features a subtle textured silicone underlay for biocompatibility and sweat resistance. The material feels medical-grade—similar to augmentation interfaces. Minimal texture, maximum skin contact for neural signal transmission.
distinctive_features: Recessed spike chamber with barely-visible seam line
Contact pad array (4 micro-points) arranged in a small circuit along the inner wrist—matte stainless steel
Subtle indicator LED (amber when armed, green when synced with neural interface) embedded in the band's edge
Fiber-optic core visible as a faint luminescent line through the semi-translucent ceramic when powered
Small pressure-release valve on the outer edge—prevents backpressure buildup
Micro-articulated spring mechanism visible as hairline indentations along the deployment axis
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Gestalt Workforce Solutions logo (interlocking geometric symbol) etched subtly into the inner wrist band. Serial number laser-burned on the underside of the band. 'DS-1 UPLOAD' designation stamped on the spike chamber's external edge in 4pt type.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained and clean—operators handle this with medical precision. Even black-market units show minimal wear because the mechanism is so refined. Occasional microscopic stress fractures around the spike chamber from repeated deployment are the only sign of heavy use.
